articles.body: You are reading the slow query log in CloudWatch Logs or a similar tool, and one query has a Rows_examined (rows read) about equal to the table's row count, or larger, while its Rows_sent (rows returned) is only a few. SHOW INDEX shows an index on the column used in the condition. Running EXPLAIN on the same query in a staging environment restored from a backup gives ALL in the type column: the whole table is read. Of the reasons MySQL can't use an index, I cover the following three. The first is a query that passes a datetime column ( created_at ) through DATE() to filter by date. I call this the "function" case.

articles.title: Ensuring type safe database queries and migrations with Node
articles.excerpt: Talking to a database with Node usually goes one of two ways: you write raw SQL and trust that the strings in your code still match the columns in the database, while dealing with SQL injections and m…
articles.body: Talking to a database with Node usually goes one of two ways: you write raw SQL and trust that the strings in your code still match the columns in the database, while dealing with SQL injections and migrations by yourself, or you pull in a full ORM and inherit an entire opinionated world just to run simple queries. Both work fine until someone renames a column and you find out about it in production, or you want to do something slightly different and your ORM just won't let you. Fortunately, there's a middle ground where you can get the best of both worlds. Writing queries with Kysely Kysely is a query builder, not an ORM. There's no entity layer, no lazy loading, no magic session flushing things behind your back.

articles.title: Did Japan Really Declare a Cyber Emergency? What Actually Happened
articles.excerpt: No. Japan did not declare a cyber emergency. You may have seen the headlines: "Japan declares first cyberspace emergency" and "AI attacks incoming." I also made a video of this. There was no legal dec…
articles.body: No. Japan did not declare a cyber emergency. You may have seen the headlines: "Japan declares first cyberspace emergency" and "AI attacks incoming." My company has run an online service in Japan for 22 years, so I read the original notices, in Japanese, the day they come out. I made a video about this, but a video can only show a few lines from each document. This article goes through the documents themselves: the ruling party's report, the government's notice, and all seven notices from the cloud provider at the center of it, including the final report that came out after I recorded the video. I also made a video of this. The short version There was no legal declaration. A politician called the situation "an emergency" at a party meeting on October 9. Nothing was switched on.

articles.title: Managing document metadata in React 19
articles.excerpt: This post's title may seem odd to you, if you're up to date, but a few things have changed from React 18 to 19, and one of them is how you manage document metadata. Before it, you likely had some shen…
articles.body: This post's title may seem odd to you, if you're up to date, but a few things have changed from React 18 to 19, and one of them is how you manage document metadata. Before it, you likely had some shenanigans going on, like react-helmet or react-helmet-async in place to dynamically update your document title, inject custom metadata, links, scripts or even styles. Thankfully, with React 19 you'll very likely be able to drop all of that in favor of simplicity and good old HTML. Managing metadata with react-helmet If you're still in the Middle Ages (React 18) you might still have react-helmet (or its fork react-helmet-async ) installed in your repository, to help you manage your document metadata.

articles.title: Total solar eclipse 2027 vs 2028 — Which one should you choose, Egypt or Australia?
articles.excerpt: From six minutes of darkness in Egypt or totality over the Australian Outback, here are the pros and cons of the next two total solar eclipses.
articles.body: For those who want to experience a total solar eclipse, the next two years present the best kind of problem. On Aug. 2, 2027, the so-called "eclipse of the century " will sweep across southern Spain, North Africa and the Middle East, bringing more than six minutes of totality to parts of Egypt. Then, on July 22, 2028, another exceptionally long total solar eclipse will cross Australia, putting the remote Outback and Sydney Harbor in the path of the moon's dark central shadow before it reaches New Zealand's beautiful South Island. Both eclipses will be spectacular, and both will require careful planning, yet they promise very different experiences.

articles.excerpt: NASA's twin ESCAPADE spacecraft are wrapping up a year-long voyage to Mars, and are now ready to make a beeline to the Red Planet.
articles.body: Twin NASA spacecraft are wrapping up a year-long escapade, ready to make a beeline to the Red Planet. The Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers (ESCAPADE) spacecraft launched in November 2025 on the second-ever flight of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket. But rather than head straight to Mars, the two spacecraft dawdled through a looping trajectory . Now, they are back in Earth's neighborhood where they tackled a crucial engine burn unusually close to Earth that — if all goes well — will set them on track for Mars . "No NASA mission has ever done this before," said Rob Lillis, a planetary and space physicist at the University of California, Berkeley and principal investigator of the ESCAPADE mission.
